9
The graph shows how quantity P varies with quantity Q for a body falling vertically downwards in
a uniform gravitational field with air resistance.
P
Q
0
0
Which pair of quantities could be represented by P and Q ?
P
Q
A
acceleration
force of air resistance
B
acceleration
time
C
velocity
force of air resistance
D
velocity
time

hints: Notice the graph is a straight line with positive intercepts where $P$ starts high and falls to zero as $Q$ increases.
For downward fall write the resultant force as weight minus air resistance, $mg - F = ma$, so think how $a$ depends on $F$.
Compare that linear $a$ against $F$ relation with the curved approach to terminal velocity expected for $a$ or $v$ plotted against time.
walkthrough: Identify the graph shape: $P$ on the vertical axis decreases linearly with $Q$ on the horizontal axis, starting from a maximum and reaching zero.
State the dynamics for vertical fall with air resistance: resultant downward force is $mg - F$, where $F$ is force of air resistance.
Use Newton's second law: $mg - F = ma$, so $a = g - F/m$.
This is of the form $a = g - (1/m)F$, a straight line of negative gradient with $a = g$ when $F = 0$ and $a = 0$ when $F = mg$ at terminal velocity.
That matches the given $P-Q$ straight line decreasing to zero, while $v$ against $t$ rises to a plateau and $a$ against $t$ decays as a curve, not a straight line. This is option A

A.explanation: From $mg - F = ma$, acceleration $a = g - F/m$ falls linearly to zero as force of air resistance $F$ rises to $mg$.

B.explanation: Acceleration against time falls with a curved gradient approaching zero asymptotically at terminal velocity, not as a straight line to zero.

C.explanation: Velocity and force of air resistance both increase together during the fall, so velocity cannot decrease as drag force increases.

D.explanation: Velocity against time increases with decreasing gradient toward terminal velocity, so the graph would rise and level off, not fall.
